pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — TERMLY EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

2. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

3. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

5. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.

6. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. going

7. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

8. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

9. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.

10. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language School.

11. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. quickly

13. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.

14. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.

15. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Phonics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
